draft.title: New technologies after 1945
card: Television spread into homes in Australia from 1956. Families could now watch news, sport and shows at home, and people spent more evenings indoors.
Early computers were huge and used mainly by governments and large firms. Over time they became smaller and cheaper, and changed how offices, banks and factories worked.
Passenger jet planes made long trips much faster and cheaper. Holidays overseas, migration and international business became easier.
The internet, widely used from the 1990s, let people send messages and find information almost instantly. It changed how people communicated, worked and spent free time.
draft.remember: New technologies changed work, communication and free time.

a.q: Why did passenger jet planes change life for many people after 1945?
opts: Long trips became faster and cheaper
Families could watch news at home
Offices could store records on computers
a.why: Jets cut the time and cost of long journeys, so overseas holidays, migration and business travel became easier. Television, computers and the internet changed other parts of life, not travel.

b.q: In 1985 a bank in Newcastle replaces its paper ledgers with computers. Which change is the most likely result?
opts: Staff do their work in new ways using machines
Customers begin to watch bank news at home
Staff travel overseas faster for meetings
Customers use the internet widely to bank
b.why: Computers changed how offices and banks worked, so staff used machines in place of paper ledgers. The internet was only widely used from the 1990s, so widespread online banking in 1985 is a tempting but wrong choice.
b.clue: Check the date against when the internet spread.

a.best: Long trips became faster and cheaper

b.best: Staff do their work in new ways using machines
